# Experimental Design

We will study how cyanobacteria hurt these insects through two pathways, poor food quality and toxicity, and how this influences the quantity, quality, and timing of insect emergence. Dietary effects will be tested by feeding the predatory larvae of emerging insects *Ischnura elegans* (damselfly) and *Chaoborus flavicans* (midge) prey (*Daphnia magna*) raised on (i) toxic poor-quality cyanobacteria (*Microcystis aeruginosa*), (ii) non-toxic poor-quality cyanobacteria (*Synechococcus elongatus*), or (iii) non-toxic good-quality algae (*Nannochloropsis limnetica*). Toxin effects will be tested by comparing predatory larvae raised on non-toxic good-quality algae with or without lysed toxic cyanobacteria. The low-quality food in the treatments constitutes 30% of the diet (70% is constituted by the medium-quality algae *Tetrademus obliquus*).
